discrepancies.title: Rent roll totals do not equal the sum of its rows: annual rent

sources.label: sum of unit rows: annual rent

discrepancies.why: The stated total is not the sum of the unit rows (it may be stale or typed over). The screen re-sums the rows and ignores the stated totals.

impact.basis: sum of rows minus stated total

discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask the property manager for a system export of the rent roll at the same date.

discrepancies.title: 3 unit(s) marked occupied with leases that ended before 2026-11-01 (108, 312, 403); 2 let unit(s) with no Ejari number (309, 405)
discrepancies.why: A tenant holding over on an expired or unregistered lease has a weaker legal position for the landlord (an unregistered contract lacks legal standing). The engine rolls expired leases at the start of the analysis; AED 339,000 of in-place rent (12.4%) sits on these units.

impact.basis: in-place rent on the affected units

discrepancies.analyst_action: Request Ejari certificates and renewal status for each listed unit.

discrepancies.title: Statement rental income AED 2,316,250 is 15.0% below rent-roll in-place rent AED 2,725,000
discrepancies.why: Physical occupancy is not economic occupancy: units on the roll are not paying in full (arrears, concessions, bounced cheques or tenants not paying). The engine applies the mandate collection loss, which is far smaller than this gap (amounts are for a 12-month period).

impact.basis: statement rental income minus rent-roll in-place rent

discrepancies.analyst_action: Request the aged receivables report and bank statements for the statement period.

discrepancies.title: OM yield 8.9% is on asking price, before 6.2% acquisition costs

sources.label: acquisition costs (DLD 4%, broker, trustee, mortgage registration)

discrepancies.why: A buyer pays AED 1,899,882 on top of the price. On price plus costs the same income gives 8.4%.

impact.basis: OM income on price plus acquisition costs, minus the stated yield

discrepancies.analyst_action: Compare deals on yield on total cost; ask the broker to restate the yield on that basis.

rejected_model_findings.title: Headline rent and 8.9% ROI appear to include vacant and disputed units at full rent

evidence.quote: ROI = total yearly rent / asking price.

rejected_model_findings.why: The OM gives one 'Total Rent' figure and calculates the 8.9% ROI from it, while also saying the building is only 92% occupied. The rent-roll check found in-place rent equal to potential rent (both AED 2,725,000). The rent roll also shows 4 vacant units, 2 units in legal cases and 1 with notice served. So the headline rent seems to include units that are not paying. The operating statement's rental income is 15% lower. The ROI is therefore likely overstated as a measure of current income.
rejected_model_findings.analyst_action: Ask the seller for a unit-by-unit schedule that separates contracted rent of paying tenants from asking rent on vacant, notice-served and legal-case units. Recompute in-place rent and yield from that schedule and reconcile it to the bank-based T12 rental income.
rejected_model_findings.rejected_because: contradicted by the rent roll: OM income AED 2,725,000 equals in-place rent AED 2,725,000 within 2%

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
The mandate verdict is **Needs work**. Every hard filter passes: asset type, freehold single title, JVC location, unit count, price band, building age, Year-1 DSCR and no related-party master lease. The deal misses three soft tests:
- going-in net yield on total cost, 5.96% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] against the 6.00% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] minimum;
- levered IRR, 3.89% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]] against the 8.00% [[mandate.target_levered_irr.threshold]] target;
- equity multiple, 1.20x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] against the 1.35x [[mandate.target_equity_multiple.threshold]] target.

Recommendation: do not take this to full diligence at the asking price of AED 30.5m [[deal.asking_price_aed]]. Re-engage only at or below our walk-away price of AED 27.54m [[uw.walk_away_price_aed]], which is 9.7% [[uw.walk_away_discount_to_asking]] under asking. The levered IRR target sets that price.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Opaline Residence, Jumeirah Village Circle (JVC), G+4, completed in 2012 [[deal.completion_year]], 48 units [[om.unit_count]]: 16 studios [[rr.studio.units]], 24 1BR [[rr.1br.units]] and 8 2BR [[rr.2br.units]].
- **Price:** AED 30.5m [[uw.price_aed]], or AED 949 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_nsa]] on NSA. On BUA it is AED 778 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_bua]].
- **Income:** in-place contract rent is AED 2.73m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]]. 44 units [[rr.let_units]] are let, giving 91.67% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] occupancy by units. All leases are direct, with no master tenant. The landlord pays the chiller.

## Returns and key metrics
| Metric | Screen | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Year-1 NOI | AED 1.93m [[uw.noi_year1]] | none |
| Going-in net yield on total cost | 5.96% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | 6.00% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] |
| Year-1 DSCR | 1.51x [[uw.dscr_year1]] | 1.30x [[mandate.min_dscr_year1.threshold]] |
| Levered IRR, pre-tax | 3.89% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]] | 8.00% [[mandate.target_levered_irr.threshold]] |

The OM headlines 8.90% [[om.yield_stated]], on asking price. The OM does not state its income basis, net income or operating costs. On the buyer's basis, Year-1 NOI over price plus acquisition costs, the yield is 5.96% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]]. Over price alone it is 6.33% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_price]].

## What would make it fail
1. **Rent and exit pricing.** There is no cushion. With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower, levered IRR is 1.21% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+0.levered_irr_pre_tax]]. Add an exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider and it is -1.02% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.levered_irr_pre_tax]]. Base rent with the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider gives 1.73% [[uw.sens.r+0.e+50.levered_irr_pre_tax]]. Only market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] higher with the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] tighter clears the target, at 8.53% [[uw.sens.r+5.e-50.levered_irr_pre_tax]]. The base-case levered exit gain is negative, AED -1.80m [[uw.exit_gain_levered_aed]].
2. **Collections.** Statement rental income is AED 2.32m [[opex.rental_income]], well below the rent roll. The statement NOI of AED 1.41m [[opex.noi_aed]] is far under our Year-1 NOI. If the statement is the true picture, the underwriting is too high.
3. **Weak leases and rollover.** Several units marked occupied have expired leases, and two let units have no Ejari number. About AED 339,000 [[disc.expired_lease_counted_occupied.impact_delta_aed]] of rent sits on them. The biggest expiry window runs from 1 May 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_start]] to 31 July 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_end]], with AED 960k [[uw.max_expiry_window_rent_aed]] of rent, or 35.23% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]]. That is inside the 40.00% [[mandate.max_lease_expiry_share_in_any_quarter.threshold]] limit but still a concentration.

## Discrepancies that matter
1. **Collections gap (high).** Statement rental income is 15.0% [[disc.collections_gap.title]] below rent-roll in-place rent, a shortfall of AED 409k [[disc.collections_gap.impact_delta_aed]]. This points to arrears, concessions or non-payment. The screen used the rent roll and applied only a 1.00% [[assume.collection_loss]] collection loss, far smaller than the gap.
2. **Expired or unregistered leases (high).** AED 339,000 [[disc.expired_lease_counted_occupied.impact_delta_aed]] of rent, 12.4% [[disc.expired_lease_counted_occupied.why]] of in-place rent, is on these units. The screen rolls expired leases at the analysis start. A tenant on an unregistered contract gives the landlord a weaker legal position.
3. **Rent roll does not foot (high).** Summed unit rows differ from the stated total by AED -233k [[disc.rent_roll_does_not_foot.impact_delta_aed]]. The screen relied on the unit rows and ignored the stated totals.
4. **OM yield excludes acquisition costs (medium).** The OM's income on price plus costs gives 8.4% [[uw.om_yield.stated_income_on_total_cost]]. Acquisition costs are 6.2% [[uw.acquisition_costs_pct_of_price]] of price.

Lower-severity items are not discussed.

## Before diligence, check
- System export of the rent roll from the property manager at the same date.
- Ejari certificates and renewal status for each unit flagged as expired or unregistered.
- Aged receivables report and bank statements for the statement period.
- The broker's restatement of the yield on total cost, plus the OM's net income, operating costs and rent basis, which it does not state.
- Title documents confirming freehold single title.

## Assumptions
Loan-to-value is 45.00% [[assume.ltv]] at 6.80% [[uw.interest_rate]] (3M EIBOR 4.30% [[assume.eibor]] plus a 2.50% [[assume.margin]] margin), amortised over 20 years [[assume.amortisation_years]]. Structural vacancy is 5.00% [[assume.structural_vacancy]]. The hold is 5 years [[uw.hold_years]], starting 1 January 2027 [[uw.analysis_start]]. The exit yield is 6.75% [[uw.exit_yield]], including 25 bps [[assume.exit_yield_expansion_bps]] of expansion. Market rent moves -4.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1 and -1.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year2]] in Year 2, then 2.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]]. These are mandate and market assumptions, not package data. No operating cost categories were filled from defaults.
